comments.text:
As a researcher in the domain, I must say I saw a real change around 2010, when hundreds of talented Chinese students came into Western universities all over the world, from Europe to the US, Canada and Australia. Chinese PhD students were part of the AI development from the beginning. Most of the major papers in the last 10 years have had at least one Chinese author. By the way, the US advantage is based on European and Asian researchers, there are very few American researchers in the domain and very few engineers, while Chinese companies only recruit Chinese nationals. The US have no moat in AI, because most of their researchers are foreigners. As someone who work in the domain, I'm sorry but what he says is not some kind of propaganda for China, it is the reality I experience everyday on the job.
In the US the brightest students become lawyers, because this is where the money is, they don't become engineers or researchers, because when you spend $20,000 a year in college, you don't want to end in a job, which starts at $60,000 with little chance of reimbursing your debt before 40. In China and in Europe, this level of debt doesn't exist, this is why people can become researchers or engineers. Nothing rings more true than the US is led by lawyers and China by engineers. Don't look forward to understand why Boeing or Intel started to crumble when they replaced their managers, who were engineers, by people who didn't understand engineering and wouldn't care less.
